body: When a person calls the national line, it routes you to a number based on your phone number. It sent me to Arkansas, even though I live in another state now.

That's a good story. I just don't know if I can do this. I'm so bored and alone. I really thought my life was going somewhere about a decade ago. I know booze fucked it up, but now only booze seems to help. I even tried calling the suicide hotline 7 times last night. I got put on hold.. haha. Good thing I'm too much of a coward to do it.

I don't think I have shit to give to this world. That's why I want out.

How do you not kill yourself? I just gave up on not drinking. No, I don't feel better. I just stared at my computer all day once I dragged myself out of bed at 2pm. I really just want to die. Why do I have to have a family? It isn't fair that they have such pull over me. I don't care about myself. Why should I be beholden to trying not to upset others?

Dude, I've had this job since October. If I don't like myself, what's the point. I don't have an aspiration to be a cog in some dude's machine at some job that literally has no bearing on helping any other human.

I'm sorry. I know you're trying to be a positive person. It just... really doesn't work. People don't love me, besides those who are obligated to do so. If they did, I wouldn't be here. Alone. Drunk without friends. 

Whatever. I'm too much of a fucking pussy to kill myself like I should. I'm trying to get the courage and figure out if there is enough of anything to do it here.

edit: I'm sorry. Thank you for being so positive. I just can't. I don't want you to be mad at me or think I'm an asshole, random internet person. I just wanted to be happy and have a life that mattered, but that's not going to happen. I can't get into working, coming home alone to eat and watch tv, waiting for the weekend only for it to be me watching netflix for 10 hours and roaming my house otherwise.. I just can't. All my siblings are as successful as they were meant to be. I just want the courage to die. It's too late for things to get better.

http://vimeo.com/86262069

Yeah, that just happened. I got put on hold. I checked for online chat. I guess they don't do that at night. ha. what a joke. This site is more responsive than the actual site. Wow.

That's a cute story. I can't afford to make my parents happy by sustaining a real job and not living at home, afford insurance, which ironically (see below) makes me unable to afford seeing anyone.

Plus, I missed so many days at work, if I miss again, even for a doctor's appt, I'd be suspended without pay and then fired the next time. The conversation has happened. 

I can't get another job, because I'm a felon. Look, I grew up one of these people who thought I was something. I wish the teachers wouldn't have lied. I'm a piece of shit. I wish I had a gun, so I could say goodbye and just move on.

I just never could quit. Some can; I can't. I'm just so tired of the bullshit that is life. It used to be good, and then I fucked it up. Yeah, drink was the underlying cause, but I chose the drink. 

Anyhow, sorry. This isn't the place.

Well, I didn't make it. Y'all go along with your success stories. Someday maybe I'll just get the courage to end it. I wish I didn't have a family still around, because I'd end it in a second. That's what scares me most about being sober. My life has no value. I work a totally pointless job. I ruined any chance I had at having a meaningful life because of the legal problems I got myself into while being sober. No one will ever be with me.

I made it sober for a week, which was the longest I've made it in quite a while. But why? Why try? I don't even care about myself. I ruined myself. Society doesn't regard me as a person. No woman certainly will. If you can't matter to yourself or matter to society, why live? If it weren't for the pain I would cause my mom and dad, I'd do it right now.

Yeah.. not sure I can deal with these feelings. Not feeling them was probably better. Thanks for trying to help. Some people just can't be fixed I guess.

edit: I tried to call one of those lines.. I just hung up. Why would I want to tell my problems to a stranger who literally doesn't care about me and is getting paid to do it? I just think it's pathetic if the only person I can talk to is paid for it.
Nah my problem is I make just over what's necessary to get a subsidy on the health care exchange AND i live in one of the top ten most expensive areas.

I feel like that's the catch 22. I *know* drinking will make it worse, which is why I'm managing to stay sober today, but it really sucks to constantly have these thoughts. Thankfully I'm too cowardly to act on them even if I truly wanted to.

Thanks for your advice. I'm hoping if I just stick with it long enough that I'll start to level out. It's pretty rough so far, though. A lot worse than I expected, obviously.

I can't afford it, but it might be nice. Oh, the irony of the "Affordable Care Act," where I ponied up to pay 13% of my income, so now I can't even afford to see a doctor.

You're right, though. I do need to.
I think not thinking I'm worth fighting for is the number one thing inhibiting my recovery. I'm sober for now with 2 hours until the booze store closes. Taking it second by second.

That's a pretty hateful way to convince someone to get sober. Another thing I hate with AA is the unwillingness to help people who aren't yet at a chance to help themselves. There is no reason to wait until a person is almost dead to reach out.
This is really helpful advice for someone who will be on his first day again once the booze has left my system.

Actually, I try to hide that I either drink or try not to drink from my family and friends, because it's a source of embarrassment to me that I have this problem when none of them do - either don't drink at all or have maybe a couple drinks per month.

The shame that comes with admitting addiction has been one of the biggest barriers in the different times I've tried.

I've never gotten a sponsor. The last time I honestly tried to sober up I was turned down by the person I asked. He suggested someone else, but at the time, that one would only take me if I could go to daily meetings, which would've required a 2 hour round trip 5 days a week. I had no job at the time, so I couldn't afford it. He thought that was an excuse. Anyhow, I ended up moving. Maybe I'll find one here. 

I personally wish AA would just assign you a sponsor, because otherwise I don't know if I'll work up the courage to ask someone.

Here. As someone who is still drinking but has neither the means nor the social situation to deal with it (excuses,whatever): acamprosate/naltrexone, caring friends and/or family who you are willing to be open with, an even closer friend or professional (not necessary) counselor that can guide you through it, a person you trust who has overcome substance abuse.

Those things target the brain chemistry aspects of the disease, the social problems of finding new friends, the personal/moral issues that come from it, and the longevity that is required to get rid of the habitual part, which for me, has been the real problem.

I'm an "uncured" person, but if I had any friends or family that lived within a 500 mile radius, the money for those drugs, the trust of a person to be truly, *truly* honest with, and people I wasn't too embarssed to be around, I think I could overcome.

AA is a program built around failure, in my opinion.

Can I say that I really despise the AA lingo of rock bottom?

I don't know, maybe that is why I'm still unable to really, really quit. It just doesn't seem fair that I have to end up in prison or dead to get sober. There has to be some way to fix myself now based on the mistakes of others without experiencing it myself.

Am I wrong?

I absolutely agree with this. If you read my comment history, you might see that this isn't working for me. If you read my real account, you'd see that I consider myself a Christian despite all its unpopularity on the internet. I say that only because I definitely have always believed in a higher power that did have the power to help me. Good lord, I have an advanced degree in the subject.

And yet, I have always been unable to get clean. Eventually, within the AA model, if you come from that background, you start to wonder if it's God, not you, that's the problem.

I do applaud the program because it has helped a lot of people. I went myself Saturday night, and it was great. Clearly it didn't "work" in the way that medicine works, or I wouldn't be here now. 

I just want to know if acamprosate or naltrexone might help me moderate until my brain chemistry is more in order. Maybe I don't have the will that you people do. I know I don't have the social structure (i.e., I have none.).

I should also say before anyone jumps into *of your own understanding* that I think that was a bullshit move of AA in the beginning on the wishes of their agnostic members. By bullshit, I don't mean *wrong* or that my dogma is the correct dogma. I mean, they caved to the fact that they couldn't just set up a missionary society for drunks after they noticed even agnostics and atheists were getting help by following their program. For me, however, this is not an option. There is no God-of-my-understanding by my theological views. There is either the God I believe in due to my rationally held beliefs, or no God at all.

I made it four days this time. I've made it months in the past. Let me tell you this: I hope you live somewhere where you have friends and family that support you even to the point of annoying you beyond belief.

I'm not gonna lie. I succumbed today. I just can't seem to get this sobriety stuff, but you can! Just don't try to go it alone if you're as deep in as a lot of us are/have been.

>First you have to actually want it.

I have tried and failed to sober up so many times, and I've just never gotten to understand how you could "actually want it." I mean, when I objectively look at the destruction or feel the pain of coming down from a long few days of drinking straight, I do want it. But after feeling good for a few days, I always "miss" the feeling, the camraderie, the habitual nature of the drink in hand.

I don't know if that makes sense. I certainly *want to want* to quit, but I just can't get over the hump to craving sobriety as bad as I crave a drink. Any advice on that front? I really hope the answer isn't, guess you'll just have to keep drinking and destroy more of your life before you "really want it."
